notes.text: The witness directly names Rabbi Hillel son of Rabbi Vallas in the case of shared ownership.
The exact report alternates Rabbah son of Rava and Hillel son of Vallas.
The same attribution pair appears in the voting procedure.
The passage distinguishes the notebook and wall transmission chains, with the name Alas in both.
The close of chapter 2 gives the Vallas form and Hillel asking his father.
The garment costs thirty myriads of dinars. The clause about giving it to Rabbi is parenthetical in this digital version.
The form Hillel ben Hallis is in halakhah 3, segment 5, of the checked version. Retain Heilprin’s printed halakhah label separately.
The checked Jerusalem Talmud gives Lil son of Alas in the passage on making noise. The Vilna transcription gives Alam.
The companion statement separately explains Joshua’s relation to Elazar. The source does not establish that Hillel and Rabbah are the same person.
The corresponding continuation distinguishes Joshua from Elazar when explaining why they are excluded.
The dedicated entry prefers Vallas to Valus and attributes that distinction to Rashi.
Heilprin explicitly sends his separate Lil entry back to Hillel. That is Heilprin’s identification.
This parallel transcription gives Alam in the clapper passage. Keep the Alas reading of the other witness visible.

Yisa and Assi remain Heilprin’s proposed reading and identification. The checked Kilayim notebook report gives Yose. The notebook and wall transmission chains do not settle the proposed identification.
The terminal Haomer locator remains unresolved. The late Bavli Kiddushin and checked Jerusalem Kiddushin chapter did not yield the named exchange in the cited form.
Digital and printed halakhah divisions differ. The direct reading was found under Challah 1:3:5. The locator in Heilprin is retained alongside the exact digital link.
